content.text: By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
Describe how acid rain is formed
Explain the effects of acid rain on the environment
Describe methods to reduce acid rain
Write equations for the formation of acid rain

is rain that has been made acidic by pollutant gases, particularly sulfur dioxide and nitrogen oxides. Normal rain is slightly acidic (pH ~5.6) due to dissolved carbon dioxide, but acid rain can have a pH as low as 4 or even 3.

Remove SO₂ from power station emissions
Wind, solar, nuclear don't produce SO₂
Convert NOₓ to N₂ in vehicle exhausts
Design combustion to produce less NOₓ
Add calcium hydroxide to neutralise acid
SO₂ emissions reduced by 70-90% in many countries
Lakes and forests recovering in some areas
Write equations to show how sulfur dioxide leads to acid rain.
This sulfuric acid falls as acid rain
Describe the effects of acid rain on a lake ecosystem.
The pH of the lake decreases (becomes more acidic)
Fish and other aquatic animals cannot survive in acidic water
Most fish die when pH drops below 4.5
Insects, snails, and other invertebrates are affected
Acid rain dissolves aluminium from surrounding soil
Aluminium ions wash into the lake
Aluminium is toxic to fish (damages gills)
Species that feed on fish are affected
In severe cases, the lake becomes "dead"
Explain how limestone buildings are damaged by acid rain.
Limestone is made of calcium carbonate (CaCO₃)
Acid rain contains sulfuric acid and nitric acid
These acids react with calcium carbonate:
The surface of the building erodes
Details of carved stonework are lost
Historic buildings and monuments are particularly affected
Describe how liming can help a lake affected by acid rain.
Acid rain has lowered the pH of the lake
Fish and other organisms are dying
Add calcium hydroxide (lime) to the lake
This is a base that neutralises the acid:
pH of the lake increases (becomes less acidic)
Conditions become suitable for aquatic life
Fish and other organisms can return
Only treats the symptom, not the cause
Better to reduce SO₂ emissions at source
